examples.text: А где машинка? Где моя машинка?
examples.trans: Hey, where's the toy car? Where's my toy car?
Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: Agent/instrument noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-тель' ('-er'). Common masculine noun meaning 'fire extinguisher' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У вас нет огнетушителей на кухне.
examples.trans: You have no fire extinguishers in the kitchen.
Here is a normal fire extinguisher.

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)

meanings.en: other forms: его (gen/acc), ему (dat), им (instr), нём (prep)

meanings.note: state of hanging, takes в/на + prepositional

examples.text: Видишь, висит? — Да, он уже месяц там висит.
examples.trans: See that hanging there? — Yes, it's been hanging there for a month.
A large picture hangs on the wall.
It's been hanging outside for a month already!
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

examples.text: В прошлый раз я думала, война началась.
examples.trans: Last time I thought a war had started.

examples.text: Марина, ну опять ты со своей сгущёнкой! В прошлый раз я думала, война началась.
examples.trans: Marina, there you go again with your condensed milk! Last time I thought a war had started.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: смеяться над кем = to laugh at someone; perfective засмеяться = to start laughing

examples.trans: Don't laugh. Read me the number.

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary

examples.trans: We need to do even more.

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

подходить.gloss: to approach, to come up; to suit

meanings.note: очередь подходит = one's turn is coming up
это мне подходит = that suits me

examples.trans: Let's go, our turn in the queue is coming up.
The train is approaching the station.

examples.text: Я к печке подхожу. А он маячит перед глазами!
examples.trans: I walk up to the stove. And it dangles right before my eyes!
All right, here you go. There, look.
Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'seal, dental filling' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Это слово «пломба» часто звучит в разговоре.
examples.trans: This word 'seal' is often heard in conversation.

meanings.note: in greetings: добрый день, добрый вечер

examples.text: Добрый вечер, Вика. С Новым годом!
examples.trans: Good evening, Vika. Happy New Year!

meanings.note: на днях = in the next few days, or the other day

examples.trans: I'll call in the next few days.
Any day now, on the website.
Can I go and have a look?

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'знать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to recognise; to find out', paired with 'узнавать'.

examples.trans: I'll find out where he is.
You recognised me. Thanks for seeing me.

meanings.note: agrees in gender and case with the noun

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.
Why are we going so slowly?

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: 'что я за мэр такой' = what kind of mayor am I
Common masculine noun meaning 'interest' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Почему у вас такой интерес к ресторану?
examples.trans: Why do you have such an interest in the restaurant?
Look it up on the internet.
There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

examples.text: Слушай, Нина, это же тот самый ресторан!
examples.trans: Listen, Nina, this is that very restaurant!

examples.text: Мы рады видеть вас в нашем ресторане.
examples.trans: We are glad to see you in our restaurant.
They called from the Italian restaurant.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!
He is struggling with his doubts.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('bad').

examples.text: Я вчера ел маринованные грибы. Может, один гриб был плохой.
examples.trans: Yesterday I ate pickled mushrooms. Maybe one mushroom was bad.

meanings.note: persons leading an enterprise or agency

examples.trans: The leadership made a new decision.

examples.text: Но почему руководство нас совсем не ценит?
examples.trans: But why does leadership not value us at all?

examples.text: Это была только игра для строгого руководства!
examples.trans: That was only an act for the strict management!

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
present есть; у меня есть = I have

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'call; bell' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Генерал Круглов ждёт звонка. Будьте любезны.
examples.trans: General Kruglov is waiting for a call. If you'd be so kind.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'чальник'). Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common masculine noun meaning 'boss, head' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: + genitive: 'из мэрии' = from the town hall

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, я уже знаю. Мне звонили из мэрии.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, I already know. The town hall called me.

examples.text: В соседнем зале играет тихая музыка.
examples.trans: Quiet music plays in the neighboring hall.

examples.text: За соседним столиком сидели приятные люди.
examples.trans: Pleasant people were sitting at the next table.
To a guest at the next table.
I'm going to be mayor, understood?

meanings.note: hesitation, at the start of a sentence

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'втра').

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.
